the heat transfer and pressure drop characteristics are strongly affected by the flow regimes and NPs concentration of the nanofluid, while the size of NPs, clustering and temperature are also important.
the convective heat transfer is significantly enhanced by using nanofluid in different flow regimes.

the heat transfer enhancement in nanofluid flow is mostly reported for the turbulent flow regime and the heat transfer performance of nanoflud is strongly dependent on the flow regime, type, size, and concentration of NPs, temperature, and clustering.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enhancement in heat transfer of nanosized particles in the turbulent regime is greater than laminar and transitional regimes.
the Nusselt number enhancement for laminar flow regime is more pronounced as compared to turbulent flow regime.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the heat transfer enhancement in laminar flow regime is less than 10% and it is 20% to 50% in the transition flow regime, while the heat transfer enhancement is greater than 50% in turbulent flow regime.
the heat transfer and friction factors are highly dependent on flow regime.
the Nusselt number increases with the increase of Reynolds number, but the friction factor decreases with the increase of the Reynolds number.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nusselt number enhancement is not only a function of nanoparticle concentration, but is also a function of flow regime, type and size of NPs, temperature and clustering of NPs.
the heat transfer enhancement in turbulent flow is not as significant as that in transition flow.
the flow regime has a great impact on the thermal characteristics and the heat transfer enhancement of nanoflids.
